storylines.label: Reinforcement Learning
storylines.latest_title: Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning on Amazon SageMaker AI: A hands-on guide

prior_narrative.tldr: Reinforcement Learning is a loose grouping of RL items, not one developing story. Since Oct 12 it has collected a Qwen long-horizon agent approach and an O-RAN benchmark.
prior_narrative.whats_new: Oct 20-21 add two agentic-RL papers: calibrated rollout budgets for MCP tool-using agents, and BIRD-RL for stateful data-centric environments.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: The two newest papers are the relevant ones for agent builders: both address the cost and environment design of training tool-using models. QwenGyre (a secondary-source report) and X-RIC remain research or telecom-specific.

beats.headline: Alibaba Qwen introduces QwenGyre for elastic RL on extra-long-horizon agents
beats.summary: Reported via MarkTechPost; targets agent tasks that run far longer than standard RL rollouts.

beats.headline: X-RIC benchmarks agentic RAN controllers for reinforcement learning
beats.summary: Targets O-RAN controllers rather than LLM post-training.

beats.headline: Agentic RL for tool-using models: rollout budgets and stateful data environments
beats.summary: Two arXiv papers on cutting rollout cost and extending RL beyond tool-centric settings.

open_questions: Does calibrated rollout budgeting cut MCP-agent training cost on benchmarks beyond the paper's own?
Does BIRD-RL's gain on small language models hold on larger models?
Does Qwen publish QwenGyre weights, code, or benchmarks that show the elastic RL gain on long-horizon agent tasks?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: If you train tool-using models, read the rollout-budget paper for ways to skip groups with identical rewards; wait for Qwen's primary QwenGyre release before planning around it.

storylines.label: Retrieval Execution
storylines.latest_title: Context Engineering (Agent Memory) for AI Agents Starts with Retrieval

prior_narrative.tldr: Oct 6 and Oct 9 papers studied how agents pick skills and tools: one optimizes skill injections to survive routers, the other adds execution-time reliability to tool retrieval. The common thread is that agent retrieval is judged on what happens at execution, not only on semantic match.
prior_narrative.whats_new: EPGM, posted Oct 17, applies the execution lens to agent memory: it adds execution provenance to budgeted memory retrieval.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Three independent papers treat retrieval for skills, tools, and memory as an execution-time reliability problem. Relevance-only retrieval in an agent stack can pick items that are unavailable or unsafe at run time.

status.detail: Three papers on skill, tool, and memory retrieval, each tied to execution behavior; none is a shipped product.

beats.headline: Skill-router paper optimizes skill injections for retrieval and execution
beats.summary: Covers third-party skills selected dynamically by skill routers.

beats.headline: RATED adds tool availability during execution to tool retrieval
beats.summary: Targets methods that optimize semantic relevance but ignore execution-time availability.

beats.headline: EPGM brings execution provenance to budgeted agent memory retrieval

open_questions: Do any of the three papers report results on a public agent benchmark that others can reproduce?
Does any skill router or tool-retrieval library adopt execution-aware scoring?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: If your agent retrieves tools or skills by embedding similarity alone, log whether each retrieved item was actually available and succeeded at run time, so you can measure the gap these papers target.

storylines.label: DeepSeek DeepInfer
storylines.latest_title: LLMs are making formal software verification feasible at a much larger scale

prior_narrative.tldr: DeepSeek said on Oct 20 it is open-sourcing DeepInfer, the software that serves its production models. Coverage first framed it as a way to cut AI operating costs, then as pressure on OpenAI and Anthropic.
prior_narrative.whats_new: Latent Space put numbers on DeepInfer on Oct 21: 155T tokens/day per cluster at roughly 80% margin and an 81-day payback, as reported by the newsletter.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: A production-proven open inference stack gives platform teams a reference for serving cost and throughput that vLLM-style deployments can be benchmarked against.

status.detail: DeepInfer is public; independent reproduction of the efficiency claims has not appeared yet.

beats.headline: DeepSeek open-sources the stack that runs its models
beats.summary: Bloomberg, Quartz, Gizmodo and PYMNTS report the release on Oct 20 as an open-source tool to lower AI operating costs.

beats.headline: SiliconANGLE names it DeepInfer, the framework behind production services
Scale and margin figures arrive
beats.summary: Latent Space and follow-up writeups cite 155T tokens a day and a high-margin serving business.

beats.headline: Adjacent production-AI items clustered into the window
beats.summary: Not DeepSeek coverage: a QCon preview (Oct 2), GitHub secret protection (Oct 7), a recommender-systems paper (Oct 9), a mixed-hardware inference framework (Oct 18), llm-d 1.0 (Oct 20), an AWS multi-agent post (Oct 21) and an Anthropic formal-verification result (Oct 22).

open_questions: Does an independent benchmark reproduce the 155T tokens/day and ~80% margin figures?
Which hardware backends does DeepInfer support outside DeepSeek's own clusters?
Which license terms govern commercial reuse of DeepInfer?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: Read the DeepInfer repo and license before changing a serving stack; treat the margin figures as unverified until someone reproduces them on non-DeepSeek hardware.

storylines.label: Large Language
storylines.latest_title: Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning for Search-State Awareness in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models

prior_narrative.tldr: This page groups arXiv papers by the shared phrase "large language models"; they do not form one developing story. They cover a security attack on speculative decoding (Oct 6), narrative-induced sycophancy (Oct 16) and hallucinations in code translation (Oct 20).
prior_narrative.whats_new: Oct 21 adds an arXiv survey of LLM-based materials data extraction; it is a domain application, not a development of the reliability papers above it.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Each paper names a distinct failure surface: speculative decoding adds a draft-model attack path, sycophancy skews user-facing answers, and code translation adds hallucinated output in migrations. Treat them as separate checks, not one trend.

beats.headline: Hallucinations in cross-language code translation, with mitigations
Secure speculative decoding targets the draft-model path in LLM inference
LLMs applied to extracting materials data from scientific literature

open_questions: Does the speculative-decoding defense add measurable latency over unprotected drafting?
Do the code-translation mitigations hold on languages outside the paper's test set?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: Do not cite these papers as corroborating each other; if you migrate code with LLMs, add a hallucination check on translated output, and judge the other papers separately.

storylines.label: DeepSeek China
storylines.latest_title: DeepSeek Ban: China Threatens the U.S. With Countermeasures

prior_narrative.tldr: Early October coverage showed DeepSeek closing the gap with US rivals despite chip curbs, then a nearly five-hour outage on Oct 16 tied to China's chip shortage. On Oct 19 the US moved to bar it from federal agencies.
prior_narrative.whats_new: China threatened countermeasures on Oct 21 over the US federal DeepSeek ban, after Beijing publicly criticized it on Oct 20-21.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Federal contractors and anyone selling into US agencies must now treat DeepSeek models and apps as prohibited in those environments, including hosted API calls; self-hosted open weights in private stacks are a separate legal question this coverage does not settle.

status.detail: DHS ordered removal across federal agencies; China has opposed the ban and threatened countermeasures.

beats.headline: DeepSeek narrows the gap with US labs despite chip limits
Nearly five-hour outage amid China's chip shortage
beats.summary: Oct 16; recovery status is not stated in the headline.

beats.headline: DHS orders federal agencies to remove DeepSeek
Beijing opposes the ban and threatens countermeasures; open-model roundup flags new regulatory controls

open_questions: Does the ban extend to federal contractors or to self-hosted DeepSeek weights?
What countermeasures does China take, and do they touch US AI vendors?
Will other governments adopt similar restrictions on DeepSeek products?
Did DeepSeek's chip-related outage capacity problems recur after Oct 16?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: If you sell into US federal customers, audit dependencies on DeepSeek APIs and fine-tuned derivatives now, and keep a swap-in model ready.
